reason: The cited evidence shows in situ TEM observation of elastic instability in HEAs (E1) and chemical fluctuations (E2, E4), but none of the passages demonstrate the proposed integration of in situ synchrotron XRD with electron microscopy during mechanical testing, nor do they provide any support for the claimed accuracy/efficiency gains of a physics-informed ML surrogate for HfNbTiVAl10. The ML evidence (E5, E6, E7) describes standard transformer and regression models on static datasets, not physics-informed surrogates trained on in situ microstructural evolution data.
premises: In situ synchrotron XRD and electron microscopy can capture real-time microstructural evolution and local strain fields during tensile/fracture tests of HEAs.
Microstructural evolution descriptors from such in situ data can serve as effective features for ML models.
Physics-informed ML surrogates can bypass computationally intensive ab initio/CALPHAD calculations for property prediction.
This integrated approach will yield a 20-30% reduction in prediction error and 3-5x efficiency gain over traditional methods for HfNbTiVAl10.
